chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Seek refuge with Allah from the overwhelming burden of debt, the overwhelming pressure of men, and the ruin of widows.

key_terms.غَلَبَةِ الرِّجَالِ: Overwhelming pressure or dominance of men/people

ai.seo_question: What are the three things Imam al-Sadiq (as) advised seeking refuge from in this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights three distinct sources of societal vulnerability: economic bondage through debt, interpersonal dominance, and the precarious status of widows (*al-ayyim*). This triad reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on both individual spiritual protection and communal social justice, linking personal piety with the preservation of social stability. The mention of widows specifically underscores their historical vulnerability in early Islamic society, urging believers to seek refuge from their potential exploitation or ruin.
